name: Two-stage nitrogen compression with intercooling
description: Nitrogen at 25°C and 1 bar is compressed to 5 bar, cooled to 40°C, then compressed to 25 bar and cooled again to 40°C.
notes: Two-stage compression with intercooling; both intermediate pressures (5, 25 bar) are explicitly specified to detect stage-collapse (a single 1->25 bar compression puts INT1/COOLED at 25 bar). N2 stays supercritical vapour (Tc=126 K), vf=1 throughout. Independent check: per-stage isentropic-with-efficiency (gamma=1.40, eta=0.75); DWSIM lands ~2.5 C below the ideal-gas estimate (real-gas), correct direction.

name: Heat then flash n-pentane/n-octane
description: An equimolar mixture of n-pentane and n-octane at 25°C and 1 bar is heated to 75°C and flashed at 1 bar.
notes: Wide-boiling flash (pentane 36C/octane 126C): gentle T-vf slope, vf precise to +/-0.05 (Delta_vf ~0.031 per +/-2C), unlike close-boiling SAN_03/GEN_01. Independent check: Antoine+Raoult+Rachford-Rice vf 0.396 vs DWSIM 0.384 (Delta 0.012).

name: Benzene/toluene shortcut column
description: An equimolar benzene/toluene mixture is separated in a distillation column at atmospheric pressure to give 98% benzene in the distillate and 98% toluene in the bottoms.
notes: Canonical FUG shortcut column. LK=benzene, HK=toluene; 2% LK-in-bottoms, 2% HK-in-distillate; reflux R=1.3xRmin via two-pass. Fenske Nmin=8.77 (hand 8.58), Underwood Rmin=1.30 (hand 1.26). Mass balance closes EXACTLY (0.00%) with the molar-flow-fixed wrapper (05d263a); the ~4% seen in the pre-fix Stage-A probe was the mass-as-molar flow bug, not an FUG limitation.
